about: The canon: every upstream this repo is allowed to build on. Repos are pinned to a commit in upstreams.lock.json by `scripts/canon resolve`. Roles: foundation (we build on it), platform (we run on it), standard (we conform to it), tool (we run it), source (we install content from it), reference (we read it, never install it blind), watch (not adopted; tracked for convergence).

upstreams.why: The agent harness itself; its docs define every config layer this repo uses. The terminal CLI is installed at this pin and held at or above it (ADR 0022). Since ADR 0065 the pin is a floor: the CLI updates itself on the latest channel, which the settings template names, so a newer release runs before it is read here: in the background in a session with no update switch (Orca sets one in each launch that submits a prompt), or at once with claude update; a move of the pin also changes minimumVersion in home/.claude/settings.json. Moved 2026-11-11 to v2.1.322 (published 2026-11-10; its only note: fast mode on Vertex in the global, us and eu regions), the version this machine already runs.
Official library form of the Claude Code harness for headless runtime workers.
Anthropic's example skills, skill template and spec; README labels them demonstration quality.
The open Agent Skills (SKILL.md) standard adopted across agent clients.
Cross-tool agent instruction file, stewarded by the Agentic AI Foundation (Linux Foundation); Claude Code reads it via import.
Anthropic's plugin marketplace. Nothing is installed from it. It cannot be pinned as a whole, serves one SHA per plugin that Anthropic chooses, and auto-updates by default (ADR 0004).
Most-adopted community skills/workflow collection; listed in Anthropic's official marketplace. Read for patterns; not enabled without review.
Leading spec-driven workflow by adoption, but the field has not converged (Spec Kit vs BMAD vs Superpowers).
De facto ADR format; 4.0.0 is the current release.
Defines the Pinned-Dependencies and Dependency-Update-Tool checks this repo's pinning rule follows.
Anthropic's reference OpenTelemetry collector + Prometheus + Grafana setup for Claude Code telemetry.

Most-adopted local token/cost reporter; reads Claude Code's own session logs, no backend needed. Moved 2026-11-11 to v20.0.49 (published 2026-11-10; notes: 1h cache writes in JSON model breakdowns, a cline adapter, in-window counting in unified session reports, a codex parser guard, a faster claude report; nothing breaking). The version is in .claude/skills/lane-report/SKILL.md's npx command, mise.toml's comment and ADR 0008's table; the past run ADR 0007 records, scripts/test-land's fixture and scripts/check-addresses' example stay as written.

The OpenTelemetry Collector's core distribution (otelcol), which ships the OTLP receiver, the file exporter and the filter and transform processors (distributions/otelcol/manifest.yaml). It receives Claude Code's and Codex's OTLP log events on 127.0.0.1 only, keeps the three event types and the attributes scripts/lanes --rates reads, and writes them to ~/.claude/canon/otel/logs.jsonl with rotation. Installed by mise's github: backend (no mise or aqua registry entry exists), run as a launchd user agent by scripts/automation.

The status-line renderer, a Claude Code plugin (Node 22.18 or later; mise pins 24). home/.claude/canon/statusline.sh stays the configured command: it does canon's writes, then runs the newest installed version's hud.mjs from the marketplace user settings enable (the plugin's own launcher would run the newest copy from any marketplace) and shows its lines, with terminal hyperlinks removed and e-mail addresses, the repository owner and the home user name scrubbed; with the plugin absent or failing it shows canon's own line. Its logic runs under Node's permission model with an import fence that refuses network modules (fence.mjs, hud.mjs); git's status read runs with protocol.allow=never and every git call with GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH. It writes its own data folder and, on each render, heartbeat.json with the status-line input (mode 600) under ~/.claude/plugins/claude-hud/. It reads the status-line input, the transcript, ~/.claude.json's oauthAccount (shown only by showAuth/showAuthUser, both off in canon's claude-hud.json), CLAUDE.md, rules and settings. The plugin brings one skill, /hud, whose install step rewrites statusLine and is not to be run here. v0.15.0 is the newest tag; later release commits (0.15.3) are untagged.

Pinned, lockfile-backed tool versions installable without sudo. Moved 2026-11-11 to v2026.11.6 (published 2026-11-10, the newest published release; tag v2026.11.7 exists with no release and is not taken). Notes against v2026.11.5: mise run --multi, unprefixed [bootstrap.packages] keys, npm tools from HTTPS tarballs, named daemon ports, launchd resource limits, history.lock_wait; changed: the default prompt theme is now base16; fixes to TOML task usage, MISE_ORIGINAL_CWD with --cd, mise env --dotenv quoting, undefined env template errors (which no longer list every variable name) and command wrappers during installs. Nothing touches the keys mise.toml uses. The version is in scripts/bootstrap (MISE_VERSION), .github/workflows/ci.yml (the mise-action version input) and ADR 0008's table; the observations recorded under 2026.11.5 (home/.claude/canon/paper-session.sh, scripts/canon's self-test fixture, the trials of ADRs 0029, 0033, 0040, 0050 and 0069) stay as written. The machine's mise moves with mise self-update; the maintenance agent does not run it.
Python project/venv manager; the install path NautilusTrader itself recommends.

Backtest + live engine sharing one strategy codebase. v2 is the line upstream docs describe; still a release candidate. Held 2026-11-10: v2.0.0rc9 (pre-release, published 2026-11-10) lists 89 breaking changes; the five that touch names this repository uses are in ADR 0009's Evidence and are the scope for reading it against the adapter before it moves. Look again 2026-11-13.
Last stable v1 release; v1 now receives critical security backports only (branch develop_v1). Fallback if v2 stable slips.
Alpaca's official Python SDK; the older alpaca-trade-api-python was archived on 2026-06-17.

The HTTP library alpaca-py's REST clients use; already installed as alpaca-py's dependency, now imported directly by the Alpaca adapter for a transport adapter that gives every request a default timeout, which alpaca-py does not set (ADR 0039). The version is the one uv.lock already held.
Alpaca's official MCP server (v2 is a full rewrite). Not enabled: it selects live trading from one environment variable and its default toolset includes close-all and cancel-all.

Alpaca's official SKILL.md set. The four trading skills were read at this commit and none is enabled: unpinned installs, live switches by environment variable, safeguards that are instructions only (ADR 0004).
Alpaca's official plugin marketplace for Claude Code, Cursor and Codex. Contents not read; not enabled.
Official Go CLI for the Trading API, labelled Alpha Preview upstream; not adopted until it leaves alpha.
Community Alpaca adapter for NautilusTrader: 0 stars, no releases, unreviewed. Reference only.
Community Alpaca adapter for NautilusTrader: 0 stars, self-described alpha, unreviewed. Reference only.
Test runner. NautilusTrader's own testing guide prescribes pytest free functions and fixtures, and pytest's docs define the tests layout this repo uses.
Python linter and formatter. NautilusTrader lints and formats with it, so adapter code matches upstream style.

Type checker. Beta upstream (0.0.x, no stable API) and the field is contested; chosen because it is the one type checker NautilusTrader runs at all, though only on its examples, and held to an exact pin.

upstreams.why: Static analysis for the shell scripts and hooks, which are most of this repo's own code and run machine-wide.
Secret scanner. A trading repo handles API keys; nothing with a credential may reach a commit.
Checks GitHub Actions workflow files locally, which is the only check a workflow can get before the repo has a remote.
Checks the repo out in CI. Referenced in the workflow by commit SHA.
Installs in CI exactly the tools mise.lock records, so CI and this Mac run the same versions. Referenced in the workflow by commit SHA.
37signals' local-CI practice: run the checks on your own machine and mark the commit green with a `signoff` status. scripts/land follows the convention; the tool itself is not installed.

GitHub's own dependency update service. It reads .github/dependabot.yml and opens pull requests for the indirect packages in uv.lock and for the workflow's actions. GitHub runs it at a version this repo cannot choose, so the pin records the source that was read, not a release.

The cockpit Claude Code sessions run in: one git worktree and agent terminal per task, in one window. It starts the installed claude, so this repo's settings, hooks and instructions apply unchanged, and it reads orca.yaml for the worktree setup command. The app auto-updates by default on its stable channel, about a release a day, so this repo does not choose the version that runs; the entry follows main, and the docs it cites were read at v1.4.255. Its bundled skills orca-cli and orchestration are used within the limits of ADR 0021. It also loads a Claude Code plugin of its own, orca-agent-view, into each terminal session it starts; ADR 0023 says what that plugin does, why it stays on, and the risk it carries.

OpenAI's Codex CLI, a second agent runtime from another model family, used only as an Orca worker that reads a change and reports findings: an additional reader beside /code-review that never edits, lands or blocks (ADR 0043). Installed machine-level (mise use -g codex@<pin>, aqua:openai/codex), not in mise.toml; check with codex --version. Upstream tags about eight rust-vX.Y.Z-alpha.N pre-releases per stable release; scripts/canon outdated ignores them for this stable pin. Moved 2026-11-11 to rust-v0.167.1 (released 2026-11-10; two commits against rust-v0.167.0: opt-in incremental tools for the regular OpenAI Responses provider, and legacy incremental tools restricted to Amazon Bedrock providers; nothing under codex-rs/otel, so the event names home/.codex/otel.toml and ADR 0007 rest on are unchanged). This machine ran 0.167.0 when the pin moved; its binary moves with mise use -g codex@0.167.1 once the pin is on main.

upstreams.why: Meta's Muse Code CLI, a review-only Orca worker from another model family (ADR 0045, under ADR 0043's terms). No public repository, so no lock pin: version 1.4.15-R8339.1, installed machine-level by the owner through mise's muse tool (requested as latest), which reads Meta's muse-stable channel, a channel that publishes only the current release, so the next mise upgrade moves it; not in mise.toml; check with muse --version. Approval and an OS sandbox are on by default, a Read-only profile exists, and --yolo turns approval and sandbox off.

upstreams.why: Google's Antigravity CLI (agy), a review-only Orca worker from another model family (ADR 0045, under ADR 0043's terms). Installed machine-level by the owner (aqua:google-antigravity/antigravity-cli), not in mise.toml; check with agy --version. Its background self-updater moved it from 1.5.3 to 1.5.5, and the pin followed after the release notes of 1.5.4 and 1.5.5 were read (Auto mode for agy acp, a swarm preview, fixes; nothing that changes a review-only reader). Its troubleshooting page documents AGY_CLI_DISABLE_AUTO_UPDATE=true, set in the shell profile, to stop the updater; ADR 0065 keeps the updater on (reversing ADR 0045), so the pin is the version last read, and scripts/bootstrap --install removes the line an earlier run wrote to ~/.zshrc. Orca sets the variable in each Antigravity launch that submits a prompt, so its workers do not update; agy update does it at once.

DeepSeek Harness (npm @deepseek-ai/dsh), the engine under dsh-tui, a review-only Orca worker from another model family (ADR 0045, under ADR 0043's terms). Every tag is a pre-release. Installed machine-level by the owner (npm:@deepseek-ai/dsh 0.2.1-rc.3, with pnpm for its profile), not in mise.toml; check with dsh --version. Seven community plugins and two of its own hook packages installed machine-level into the dsh-tui profile, chosen for workflow from a community list that is not a review: aegis 2.14.2 (GanyuanRan/Aegis at commit 0461c211e4d8, MIT), dsh-doublecheck 0.9.29 (PerryLink, Apache-2.0), dsh-advisor 0.6.4 (omdsh-dev, MIT), dsh-github-skills 0.2.1 (Starfie1d1272, Apache-2.0), dsh-llm-fallbacks 0.6.12 (omdsh-dev, MIT by its LICENSE file; npm gives none), dsh-memento 0.5.28 (PerryLink, Apache-2.0), dsh-tui-find 0.5.2 (xiaoxiaohaigui, MIT), and the hook packages @deepseek-ai/dsh-hooks-claude-code and @deepseek-ai/dsh-hook-protocol 0.2.1-rc.3 (deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness, MIT). Versions and licences from the profile's installed package files; none was read beyond them. Held 2026-11-10: dsh-v0.2.2-rc.1 (2026-11-04; needs Node >=24.9) moves only with the hand-installed engine: after the owner upgrades it and dsh-tui and scripts/bootstrap --check still shows the review patch ok, both pins move in one pull request (ADR 0045 Evidence). Look again 2026-11-13. Since the proposed ADR 0086 the machine carries two named configurations beside stock: the review configuration adds @deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-terminal-bundle 0.2.1-rc.3 to the dsh-tui profile, an addition whose own source was not read here, so what it keeps and what it opens is UNVERIFIED; the build configuration is `dsh --profile headless -`, a one-shot runner carrying aegis, dsh-doublecheck 0.9.30, dsh-memento 0.5.30 at writePolicy auto, dsh-subagent-codex and dsh-subagent-claude-code 0.2.1-rc.3. Neither configuration has an eval run, so both are UNVERIFIED. The desktop surface at 0.2.2-rc.1 is interactive and reviews nothing.

Community terminal interface for DeepSeek Harness, the program Orca launches for it (dsh-tui .) under agent id dsh (its CLI bundle); which versions Orca's fixtures used is UNVERIFIED; 0.17.0 follows dsh 0.2.1-rc.3 (ADR 0045). Installed machine-level by the owner (npm:@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui 0.17.0), not in mise.toml; its profile lives in the user's home and its update command updates the profile and aligns the launcher, outside the pin. Its profiles send session logs to the configured base URL by default (session-log-deepseek.enabled, true); its configuration page at v0.17.0 documents a user profile patch row that sets it false, which scripts/bootstrap --install adds to the dsh-tui profile with the dsh-memento row memento.enabled false (ADR 0045). Held 2026-11-10: v0.19.0 (2026-11-06) keeps the user patch format and is validated against dsh 0.2.2-rc.1; it moves only with the hand-installed version: after the owner upgrades it and deepseek-harness and scripts/bootstrap --check still shows the review patch ok, both pins move in one pull request (ADR 0045 Evidence). Look again 2026-11-13.

DeepSeek Harness plugin that adds the CI run's allowlisted metadata (provider, repository, refs, commit, workflow, job, run id and URL) as one user message on a turn's first step, read from fixed environment fields; outside CI it does nothing. Its source at the pin makes no network call, writes no file and keeps nothing across sessions, so it may run in the reviewer arm (ADR 0072 rule 6). Installed only into a throwaway DSH_HOME profile, never ~/.dsh or a profile in use (ADR 0072 rule 5). Override of the host's compatibility guard: its peer range for dsh-agent and dsh-llm is ^0.1.0-rc.6, which excludes the pinned dsh 0.2.1-rc.3, so dsh refused the install (judged after the git fetch, then the profile restored) ("Running it may cause crashes or data loss") until the exact-version exemption dsh offers was granted in that profile alone (ADR 0094). A named configuration, UNVERIFIED until the review and build evals score it; a crash or data loss there retires it.

Package manager dsh-tui needs to build and update its profile (ADR 0045). Installed machine-level by the owner (mise pnpm 10.34.9), not in mise.toml; check with pnpm --version. It runs on the machine-level mise node, 24.22.2 by mise ls -g; the node entry is this repo's own request, which the same release meets. Held 2026-11-10: v12.19.0 (published 2026-11-10) is two major versions past v10. The v11.0.0 notes (2026-04-28) require Node 22 or later, turn on strictDepBuilds, blockExoticSubdeps and a one-day minimumReleaseAge by default, replace the build-dependency settings with allowBuilds, and read .npmrc for auth and registry only. Among the v12.0.0 notes (2026-08-26): git dependencies on known hosts resolve through HTTPS, an unrecognised pnpm-workspace.yaml setting fails where the project's pnpm pin is satisfied, --frozen-lockfile false is gone, engineStrict is stricter, and cyclic peer dependencies re-key a lockfile once. dsh-TUI at v0.17.0 and v0.19.0 asks for pnpm 10 or newer (docs/getting-started.en.md: 'CI uses 11'), so the pinned 10.34.9 is inside its range; its package.json pins packageManager pnpm@11.21.0, and its README documents pnpm 11's blocked install scripts, which its update command configures. Its CI runs only pnpm 11 (newest v11 tag v11.28.11), so v12 with dsh-tui is UNVERIFIED. Pin and hand install move together. mise's minimum_release_age (ADR 0008) does not filter an exact version such as pnpm@12.19.0 (mise settings page), so it would not hold a hand install. No record sets a waiting period for a pin moved by hand (ADR 0016's seven days is the bot's; ADR 0001 only quotes Dependabot's default). Re-read 2026-11-11 and still held: dsh-tui is its one consumer here (the OmniRoute gateway installs through mise's npm backend, not pnpm), dsh-tui stays at v0.17.0, and dsh-TUI's package.json at v0.19.0 still pins packageManager pnpm@11.21.0. Move it with the dsh pins, to the v11 line dsh-TUI's CI runs, not to v12. Look again by 2026-12-10, ADR 0045's review-by.

GitHub CLI, called by scripts/land, scripts/automation, scripts/survey-github and the landscape watch hook; mise.toml requests latest and mise.lock fixes the exact release.

Computes the deflated Sharpe ratio that gates a ranking (ADR 0010, computed per ADR 0031): measures.expected_max_sharpe_ratio, probabilistic_sharpe_ratio and deflated_sharpe_ratio follow Bailey and Lopez de Prado (2014), eqs. 1-2. The gate calls only those three; the test also reads its mean, standard_deviation, skew and kurtosis. Moved 2026-11-10 from v1.12.8: v1.12.9's notes list two prior-model fixes and type-check rules updated for ty 0.0.100; in the files this repository reads, measures/ and population/ are unchanged and portfolio/_base.py, portfolio/_portfolio.py and utils/stats.py change only in ty: ignore comments. A move touches pyproject.toml and uv.lock (uv add skfolio==<version>), src/canon_trading/ranking.py, returns_matrix.py and ledger.py, tests/test_deflated_sharpe.py, docs/architecture.md (the returns-matrix and gate rows) and ADR 0031's version lines; the past reads ADRs 0032, 0035 and 0041 record, and measurements a module header dates to a version, stay as written.

Holds the trial ledger ADR 0010 asks for (ADR 0035): a study in a local SQLite file through RDBStorage, one trial per backtest through ask and tell. A trial is asked for before its run and told FAIL by this repo's code if the run raises; Study.trials returns every state, so N is read back; user attributes hold each trial's config and daily returns.

Carries the dates of the returns matrix (ADR 0010 step 2): skfolio's Portfolio reads observation dates only from a DataFrame, and Population.returns_df joins them. Used to index each trial's series, drop closed days and trim to the common range; no statistic is computed with it.

upstreams.why: Context database for agents (memory, resources, skills) with documented Claude Code, Codex and DeepSeek Harness integrations. Watched, not adopted (ADR 0051): by default its Codex and DSH plugins capture turns and tool results and recall memory across sessions and other workspaces, which would carry one review into the next; pre-1.0, with six migration items in v0.5.4; its server calls an embedding and a VLM provider. Its own benchmarks are conversational memory and tau2-bench, not code review. Its DSH plugin is verified to DSH 0.2.1-rc.3.

OmniRoute (npm omniroute), a local OpenAI-compatible gateway, adopted on the owner's word to start GPT and other non-Anthropic runtimes through one endpoint (ADR 0056). No Anthropic or Claude credential, account or model is configured in it; Claude Code keeps its own login. Installed only on request, from mise's gateway config environment: mise.gateway.toml, locked in mise.gateway.lock with its npm dependency graph under .mise/locks/mise.gateway/ (mise -E gateway install --locked npm:omniroute). No mise field: scripts/canon lint reads mise.toml alone, so scripts/test-lanes holds mise.gateway.toml's version to this pin, and scripts/bootstrap --check compares the installed version with it. Started on demand by mise -E gateway run omniroute:serve with its settings fixed in that task and its storage key read from the login keychain. The repository was renamed from diegosouzapw/OmniRoute; the pin is at or above both fixes for GHSA-hf57-cqmx-p4gr (3.8.49 and 3.8.50).

Agent Orchestrator (AO), a local desktop workspace that runs a daemon and gives each task its own agent, branch and worktree: a host in the same class as Orca (ADR 0018). Not adopted; nothing installed or imported. Its docs say the npm CLI @aoagents/ao is frozen at 0.10.0, though the npm registry lists 0.10.3 as latest; the repository publishes nightly pre-releases several times a day beside stable tags about every two or three days. Permission model and cost tracking are UNVERIFIED (its migration page covers neither).

Gas City, an orchestration-builder SDK for software factories of coding agents, with work held as beads in Dolt: a framework, not a desktop host (ADR 0018). Successor to Gas Town (gastownhall/gastown), which its author's page calls retired (the repository still receives commits). Not adopted; nothing installed or imported. Its v1.5.1 notes (24 Oct 2026) mention a fix to Claude permission prompts and cost estimates for the Claude 5 family; its release notes also name Claude's builtin permission_mode "unrestricted" as a default; its permission model is otherwise UNVERIFIED.
